oil.summary: Crude prices were hammered on Monday, with Brent shedding 7.45% to $83.41/bbl and WTI off 5.67% to $79.87/bbl, as President Trump announced he was calling off a planned strike on Iranian energy sites, pulling a significant geopolitical risk premium out of the market. RBOB gasoline led the complex lower at -8.21%, with Trump publicly pressuring U.S. oil companies — naming Chevron's CEO specifically — to cut pump prices in the wake of the futures sell-off. The move reverses a sharp month-long rally of over 16% in both benchmarks. Geopolitical noise remains elevated: Iran has warned its oil blockade continues until attacks end, Ukraine struck three Russian refineries and sank a Rosatom vessel deep inside Russian territory, and dark-tanker transits at Bab el-Mandeb are surging as Houthi threats to Saudi crude shipments persist.
drivers: Trump's decision to suspend planned strikes on Iranian energy sites triggered a sharp unwind of the geopolitical risk premium across the crude complex
Ukraine's intensified drone campaign has driven Russian crude processing to a 24-year low in July, striking refineries, tankers, and pipelines
Iran's oil blockade remains in force and Houthi threats at Bab el-Mandeb continue, keeping supply-route risk elevated despite today's price collapse

gas.summary: European and U.S. gas markets diverged sharply today. TTF fell 2.15% to €57.8/MWh as Trump's Iran de-escalation — specifically calling off strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure — removed a near-term supply shock premium that had built over the past month, during which TTF had surged 31.32%. Henry Hub edged up a modest 0.76% to $2.768/MMBtu, remaining broadly flat on the week and down 13.39% over the month, suggesting U.S. fundamentals are driven by domestic factors rather than geopolitics. On the supply side, Australia's Northern Territory regulator is pushing for stricter pollution reporting rules at Santos- and Inpex-operated LNG plants in Darwin, a development that could add compliance costs to two major LNG export facilities over the medium term.
drivers: Trump's suspension of planned strikes on Iranian energy sites drove TTF sharply lower as the Middle East supply-disruption premium unwound
Henry Hub was little changed on the day and week, reflecting U.S. market insulation from geopolitical risk; the month-on-month decline of 13.39% points to softer domestic fundamentals
Australian regulators proposing tougher emissions rules for Darwin LNG plants (Santos, Inpex) adds a medium-term compliance risk to key Asia-Pacific LNG supply

power.summary: The Power & Carbon complex was relatively contained today. EU Carbon (EUA) dipped a marginal 0.25% to $76.82/EUA, broadly stable on both a daily and monthly basis, with no carbon-specific headline catalysts. TTF's 2.15% decline dragged on gas-fired generation economics but the EUA market appeared largely unresponsive. The dominant headline for the sector was Shell's agreement to sell its European onshore renewables portfolio to TotalEnergies, a strategic retreat by Shell toward its core hydrocarbon business. Separately, a reported drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant briefly pushed oil to a two-week high earlier in the session before Trump's Iran pivot reversed the move. Strait of Hormuz talks between Iran and Oman are reportedly nearing completion, which could ease regional power and gas supply risks if successful.
drivers: Shell's sale of its European onshore renewables portfolio to TotalEnergies signals a continued strategic pivot away from low-carbon power assets by the UK supermajor
A drone attack on a UAE nuclear power plant added a brief geopolitical spike to energy markets before Trump's Iran reversal dominated sentiment
Iran-Oman talks on the Strait of Hormuz reportedly nearing completion, with potential to reduce tail-risk for European gas and power supply if a deal is reached
